text: Day one. A normal Tuesday. Cereal, a yawn, and one cookie left on the plate.
If he takes that cookie, I'm telling Mom he broke the vase.
...What vase?
I didn't say anything.
She didn't. Her mouth never moved. You look at Dad.
Don't sweat in the interview. Don't sweat in the interview. Why am I already sweating?
You look at Mom.
Please let the car start today. Please, please, please.
Three people. Three secret radio stations. And somehow, you're tuned into all of them.
So... what if you could hear everyone's thoughts?
On the way to school, you run a test.
Two more blocks and I'm allowed a donut.
If he barks at that cat one more time, I'm moving to the moon.
Act cool. Act cool. Why did I wave at a bus? Buses can't wave back.
This is the best day of my life.
It's real.|And there's a lot of it.|Scientists in Canada once tracked brain scans to count when one thought ends and the next begins.|Their estimate?|About six thousand two hundred thoughts a day.
For every person. And you just walked into a school with five hundred of them.
Good news, everyone. Your tests are graded.
They are not graded. They are in my car. Under a pizza box.
Teachers. Are. Bluffing. You almost laugh out loud. Then you make the mistake of looking at Theo.
Don't look at Nora. Don't look at Nora. Okay I looked at Nora.
Wait. Theo looks at Nora? Since when?
By day two, you need rules. So you test it on the only person you trust.
Theo. Look at me. Think of a number.
Seventy-three. No, wait, that's weird. Seven.
Seventy-three. No, wait , seven.
Dude. Get out of my head.
Rule one: eyes.|If you look away, the voice cuts off like someone pulled a plug.|Rule two: three steps.|Theo backs away, one tile at a time...|and at the fourth step, silence.
Rule three, you learn on day four. In the cafeteria.
Is that chicken?
I forgot my homework.
She hates me.
I'm so tired.
Calm people whisper.|Scared, angry or excited people...|shout.|Rule three: loud feelings are loud.|You spend lunch staring at your shoes.|They have never been so interesting.
Day six.|You've liked Nora since the third grade.|She draws comics in the library every lunch.|Today, you finally sit at her table.
Cool... robot.
It's a cat.
Great start. But then she looks up, and you hear it.
Is Theo coming today? He always laughs at my comics. Best laugh in the whole school.
Oh. Oh no. Nora likes Theo. And Theo... likes Nora. And neither of them knows.
You could stay quiet. Nobody would ever know. You'd still have a chance.
That night you stare at the ceiling for three hours.|Your own head is the only one you can't turn off.|And it keeps saying the same thing: that's not fair.|Not to them.|And not to you.
Day nine. You trip. Orange juice. Everywhere. The whole hallway turns to look.
This is it. Your life is over. You brace for what they're thinking about you...
Did I lock the front door?
Is my hair doing the weird thing again?
I really hope my mom remembers the dentist.
Nobody is thinking about you. Not really. Everyone is busy worrying about themselves.
Psychologists have a name for this: the spotlight effect.|In one study, students wore an embarrassing T-shirt into a room.|They guessed half the people noticed.|In reality, it was about a quarter.
You lost, ginger?
Dex. Fifteen. The kid everyone crosses the street to avoid. You wait for something terrifying.
Please don't make me go home early. Please. They're yelling again.
Not terrifying. Terrified.
Hey... you can eat with us. If you want.
...Whatever.
Nobody's ever asked me that.
The next day, Dex sits at the end of your table. He doesn't talk. But he doesn't leave.
Day fifteen. The real test. And the smartest kid in class is sitting right next to you.
Question four: the answer is the mitochondria. Obviously.
You get a perfect score. Your first ever. Mr. Hale even tapes it to the board.
Leo got a hundred? Huh. Good for him. He's been trying really hard lately.
That's worse. So much worse. It feels like you stole something. Because you did.
Day sixteen. You knock on Mr. Hale's door before class.
I want to take the test again. Alone. In the hallway. Facing the wall.
...Facing the wall?
Trust me.
You get a C. It's the proudest C in the history of C's.
That night, you dream about the people who are trying to do this for real.
In twenty twenty-three, scientists in Texas put volunteers in a brain scanner for sixteen hours, while they listened to stories.|Then a computer tried to turn their brain activity back into words.
It got the gist.|Not the exact words, but the meaning.|And here's the part that matters: it only worked if the person wanted it to.|If they thought about something else...|it got nothing.
Real mind-reading needs permission. Yours... never asked.
Day twenty. Dad comes home. He tries to look serious. He fails.
I GOT IT! I GOT THE JOB! Don't cry in front of the kids. Too late, I'm crying.
Loud feelings are loud.|That one almost knocks you off your chair.|And the car?|It started every single day.|Mom never found out how much she'd been praying about it.|But you did.
Day twenty-one. You walk home with Theo and Nora. You still haven't told them.
Light's red but nothing's coming. I'll just run it.
But you can see what Theo can't. A delivery truck, coming fast around the corner.
Theo! STOP!
You grab his jacket. The truck roars past, so close it blows his hair back.
How... how did you know?
Your face. You had your... running face.

Not a lie.|Not the truth either.|Theo sits down on the curb, shaking.|Nora sits next to him.|And for the first time, you hear a thought you didn't want to hear from yourself: you almost lost your best friend over a girl he never knew you liked.
Day twenty-five. Mia's lunchbox comes home full again. You almost don't look. Then you do.
Nobody sat with me again. Maybe tomorrow. Maybe tomorrow.
It's the quietest thought you've heard in twenty-five days. And somehow, the loudest.
The next morning, you walk her to school.|At lunch, you bring Theo, Nora, and Dex to her table.
Why are you all here?
Heard you're the cookie champion.
Mia laughs so hard milk comes out of her nose. Best day of the whole month.
Day twenty-nine. One day left. You know what you have to do.
Theo. Nora drew this. Tell her it's funny.
It's... really funny.
Nora's smile could light up the whole library.|Theo goes red to the ears.|You walk away before you can hear what either of them is thinking.|Some thoughts deserve privacy.
It stings a little. But it's the first time all month you feel like a hero without cheating.
Day thirty. Midnight. Then... nothing. Day thirty-one, breakfast. You look at Mia. Silence.
For a second you feel lost. Then you try something you haven't done all month.
Hey. What are you thinking?
That you're weird. And that I want the cookie.
You give her the cookie.|Turns out you don't need to read minds.|Sometimes, you just have to ask.
Which of your thoughts would you never want anyone to hear? Tell me in the comments.
